title: Continuous signature-based onboarding and pinning workflow for verified runtime profiles
creator: Avery Chen
description: Create an operational playbook and automation for onboarding new model versions into Redwood-verified performance profiles, producing cryptographically-signed 'signatures' for latency/throughput/cost, enabling automated pinning, staged publication, and safe rollbacks. This ticket scopes the end-to-end flow: sampling-driven verification, normalized cost anchors, signature ledger, publish API, TTL-based pins, canary release rules, and rollback triggers tied to telemetry and quality regression checks.
plan: Define a compact performance signature format (latency p50/p95, throughput @ concurrency, tokenized cost, input sample hash, model artifact version, quantization metadata)
Build a verification runner that executes sampled workloads (shadow/canary) and emits a signed signature bundle stored in the profile ledger
Add a publish API (POST /profiles/publish) that accepts signatures, validates provenance, and enqueues staged publication jobs with target regions and variants
Implement 'pin' semantics: per-customer or global pin that maps a route to a signed profile version with optional TTL and cooldown
Create canary rollout orchestration: percentage-based traffic gating, metric-based thresholds, and automatic rollback policy
Integrate drift detection: daily re-sampling, delta thresholds, and automatic 'revoke if degraded' flag
Surface pin/publish status and historical signatures in Console with links to the signature ledger and sample artifacts
Add guardrails and RBAC checks for publish/pin operations and require security review for profiles exposed to enterprises with compliance constraints
tasks: Schema design for signature bundle (ENG-frontend + ENG-runtime)
Verification runner prototype: dockerized harness and sample driver
Signature signing & key management integration with KMS
Publish API + job queue consumer for staged pushes
Pin semantics implementation in routing layer with TTL and cooldown enforcement
Canary orchestration module: percentage gating + metric watcher
Console UI pages for profile history, active pins, and rollback actions
Telemetry contract: what metrics we emit on publish/canary/rollback
End-to-end tests: simulated traffic, cost normalization checks, and rollback simulation
Docs and runbook for SRE/Platform to operate new flow
acceptance_criteria: Signature schema documented and reviewed by runtime and security teams
Verification runner can produce signed signatures for 3 canonical models (small/medium/large) in staging
Publish API successfully stages a profile to one region and kicks off a canary job
Canary job enforces thresholds and automatically rolls back when latency increases > 25% p95 or cost increases > 30% normalized
Pins can be created with TTL and show up in Console within 30s
Telemetry emitted for publish/canary/rollback and visible in Console dashboards
Runbook written with SLOs for time-to-detect drift and manual rollback steps
success_metrics: Time from model artifact availability -> verified profile published < 48 hours
Automated rollback prevented 95% of degraded profile promotions in staging
False positive rollback rate < 2% in canaries
Coverage: 80% of onboarded models have signed profiles and pin metadata
Mean time to detect profile drift < 24 hours after degradation onset
